description:
Found while doing fz-5xp.12's first work item, which cannot land without this.

That item is "binary search in Heap::read_map_addr_value_ref (the array is
already sorted)". Two things had to be true and only one was.

FIRST, the ORDER had to agree with the EQUALITY. It did not for binary keys --
fixed in fz-5xp.48, which also turned out to be a silent wrong answer on the JIT
door.

SECOND, every map has to actually BE sorted. It is not. `Heap::alloc_map_slots`
(runtime/src/heap/imp.rs) writes entries in the order given and sorts nothing;
it is a raw writer that trusts its caller. Of its callers:

  * imp.rs:464 and imp.rs:570 sort and dedup first -- correct;
  * deep_copy.rs:100 preserves a sorted source's order -- correct for atom and
    binary keys, which are the ones that work at all (see fz-5xp.27);
  * ir_runtime.rs:1319 builds the empty map -- vacuous;
  * ir_runtime.rs:212, `fz_process_heap_alloc_stats`, hands it INSERTION ORDER.

That last one is unsorted in practice: its atom ids do not ascend with insertion
because most of those atoms were interned earlier by the compiler. Measured, a
binary search over it returns nil for `stats[:map_bytes]` while finding
`stats[:allocs]`, and 25 fixtures lost a line of output because
`stats[:list_cons_bytes] + ...` silently became nil.

The linear scan hides it: the scan uses the structural relation and never
consults the order, so an unsorted map works. That is why nothing noticed.

DONE = every map is sorted by construction, so the array is searchable. Either
`alloc_map_slots` sorts and dedups like its siblings -- one place, invariant
held by construction, at the cost of re-sorting already-sorted input on the hot
paths -- or it keeps a debug assertion that its input is sorted and each caller
is fixed. Prefer the first unless the hot-path cost measures.

WATCH OUT: sorting the stats map changes its RENDER order from insertion order
to key order, which ~25 fixtures print. That is a golden change of a different
kind from the resource reductions this epic has been reblessing freely -- it
reorders output rather than lowering a number, so it wants a deliberate look
rather than a blanket rebless. The values are identical either way.

Then fz-5xp.12's binary search is a two-line change, and it is worth having:
the search measurably cut the reductions the same program spent.
title: Not every map is sorted, so the flat array is not searchable
